tax.text: Fulcher proposed reducing income and corporate taxes as a way to encourage reinvestment and economic growth.
tax.quote: Reduce income and corporate taxes: Individuals and companies will reinvest those dollars into the economy (wiser than government does), resulting in economic growth.

wages.text: In a candidate questionnaire, Fulcher opposed raising the federal minimum wage and criticized federal wage standards.
wages.quote: No. There are all kinds of flaws with this rationale.

trade.text: Fulcher joined a letter urging Japan to end restrictions on U.S. potato exports and called international trade critical to the industry.
trade.quote: International trade and foreign export markets are critical to the U.S. potato industry

debt.text: Fulcher supports a balanced-budget amendment and says Congress must control spending to address the national debt.
debt.quote: I have always supported a constitutional amendment for a balanced budget.

schools.text: Fulcher said he had continually supported school choice through his service in the state senate and Congress.
schools.quote: I have continually supported school choice through my service in the state senate and congress.

safety.text: Fulcher proposed incentivizing state and local governments to fund law enforcement through the SAFE Act.
safety.quote: The Second Amendment for Everyone (SAFE) Act incentivizes state and local leadership to fund law enforcement.

immigration.text: Fulcher supports border-wall funding, enforcement of immigration laws, and a controlled vetting process for people entering the country.
immigration.quote: I am working to put in place resources to make sure laws are enforced and we have an orderly, thorough, and controlled vetting process for anyone entering the United States.

guns.text: Fulcher opposes gun-control measures and says he will work to overturn restrictions he considers unconstitutional.
guns.quote: I will work with my Republican colleagues to overturn this constitutional injustice.

abortion.text: Fulcher says life begins at conception and describes himself as ardently pro-life.
abortion.quote: I believe life begins at conception and that every unborn child has the inherent right to life.

cannabis.text: Fulcher said he strongly opposes marijuana legalization and is spending his own money to oppose an initiative.
cannabis.quote: I strongly oppose it. Idaho should not want it.

health.text: Fulcher named healthcare reform that re-engages market forces as a priority for increasing access and lowering costs.
health.quote: healthcare reform that re-engages market forces to increase access and decrease costs

energy.text: Fulcher proposed increasing domestic energy production and preserving infrastructure he says supports Idaho jobs and the regional economy.
energy.quote: Energy is the hub of our economy, and if we bolster domestic production to once again become a net energy exporter, economic growth (and international leverage) will follow.

voting.text: Fulcher supports requiring proof of citizenship and voter ID to vote.
voting.quote: We need proof of citizenship and voter ID to vote. That’s what the Constitution requires, and we must enforce it.

tax.text: She proposes cutting taxes for middle-class Americans and small businesses while raising corporate tax rates and funding public priorities.
tax.quote: Increase corporate tax rates, remove corporate tax breaks/subsidies, and protect Idaho’s labor and resources from monopolized industries.

wages.text: She supports raising the federal minimum wage, strengthening collective bargaining, and penalizing union-busting.
wages.quote: Increase the federal minimum wage, benefit packages, overtime protections, and secure worker pensions.

trade.text: She advocates protective trade policies and expanding domestic manufacturing to help reduce building-supply costs.
trade.quote: Solid, protective trade policies, expanding American-made manufacturing markets, and building out domestic infrastructure for necessary building supplies are the structural ways we bring home prices down permanently.

debt.text: She says Social Security should be guaranteed for future generations with cost-of-living increases and calls for comprehensive Medicare coverage.
debt.quote: Social Security must be unconditionally guaranteed for future generations with automatic, real-world cost of living increases.

housing.text: She supports incentives for local builders and developers to create diverse, accessible housing opportunities.
housing.quote: We must look at aggressively revising the tax code and HUD to create solid incentives for local builders and developers; currently, broken tax breaks favor corporate developers holding on to vacant commercial lots rather than creating diverse, accessible housing opportunities.

schools.text: She supports federal funding for public education and opposes diverting taxpayer funds to private education.
schools.quote: Taking the financial responsibility off local property taxes and levies allows every school district—from rural to suburban and urban—to thrive. Not a single cent of taxpayer funds should ever be diverted to private education.

immigration.text: She supports streamlining legal immigration, expanding immigration court capacity, and stopping mass deportations.
immigration.quote: We must immediately streamline legal application processes, drastically expand the number of immigration judges and court attorneys to clear massive backlogs, and hire professional border agents for high-traffic entry points.

abortion.text: She criticizes Idaho’s post-Dobbs restrictions and says lawmakers should listen to women, families, and medical professionals.
abortion.quote: Instead, it is time for lawmakers to step out of the exam room and listen to women, families, maternal-fetal specialists, and healthcare professionals to protect lives.

health.text: She supports a universal single-payer system to provide health coverage for every American.
health.quote: Taking health insurance companies completely out of the equation and moving to a universal single-payer system is the best, most transparent, and cheapest way forward for families.

tax.text: She said higher taxes on top earners and corporations are needed to raise revenue and fund public programs.
tax.quote: We have to raise the taxes on the very high-income people — we have to. We have to raise corporate taxes.

trade.text: Her campaign platform opposes tariffs, citing higher costs and retaliation from trading partners.
trade.quote: Tariffs raise the costs of fertilizer and other raw materials, invite retaliation from trading partners, and destroy confidence in the reliability of our supply.

debt.text: She says she would reduce the national debt through higher revenue and lower expenditures, including lower payouts for the highest Social Security earners.
debt.quote: Raise revenue and reduce expenditures while we grow the economy.

housing.text: Her platform calls for building more houses and removing obstacles that increase building costs.
housing.quote: The intuitive solution to the housing shortage is the right one: build more houses.

immigration.text: She supports legal pathways for some immigrants while also calling for border enforcement and deportation of people who commit serious crimes.
immigration.quote: I support the Securing Agriculture's Workforce Act as the right vehicle for establishing a pathway to legitimate temporary worker status for the agricultural workers who are already here

health.text: Zabel rejects a wholesale single-payer shift but supports restoring ACA subsidies, reversing Medicaid coverage cuts and regulating private providers and insurers.
health.quote: A wholesale shift to single-payer clears neither bar with confidence.
